subject: Hyperqueue collapse — reserved throughput shortfall & exec intervention
messages:
From: Liam Jones <liam.jones@granitepay.com>
To: support@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-22T08:14:00Z
Subject: sudden spike — heavy 5xx and queueing (GranitePay production)

Tessa / Redwood ops,

We started seeing a large burst of 5xx errors and token queueing at 08:05 UTC. Our dashboards show reserved throughput pegged and the GPU pool queue length shooting up — latency to completion has gone from ~120ms to >3s for many calls. Affected endpoints: /v1/chat and /v1/generate (production slot).

Attached are a small sample of error lines and a screenshot of the queue-length spikes. This is impacting live payment flows — customers are retrying and some timeouts have led to transaction failures. Please escalate; we are at risk of breaching our SLA.

Key details:
- Tenant: granitepay-prod
- Reserved capacity: 45k token-units/min (committed)
- First observed: 08:05 UTC
- Error pattern: 503 / 504 + token queue backlog

Can someone confirm whether this is isolated to our pool or a broader GPU farm issue? We need ETA for mitigation and whether you can authorize burst capacity.

Thanks,
Liam Jones
Head of Platform Reliability, GranitePay

Attachment: granite-error-logs-20280522.txt
Attachment: grafana-queue-depth-20280522.png

From: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Liam Jones <liam.jones@granitepay.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, david_kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-22T08:22:00Z
Subject: Re: sudden spike — heavy 5xx and queueing (GranitePay production)

Liam — thanks for the early alert and attachments. We're looking now. Quick notes:

1) Confirmed we see the same queueing signal in our per-reserved-pool telemetry. The reserved pool serving granitepay-prod is saturated; headroom is at ~2% for the last 6 minutes.
2) 5xx pattern lines up with kernel-level OOM/backpressure retries on a subset of nodes; not every node is failing.
3) We've opened an internal bridge and notified infra.

Immediate next steps (we'll keep you posted):
- Short-term: Enable a targeted failover to a compatible model variant with lower memory footprint (approx 1.5–2x throughput improvement per GPU) while we stabilize — requires authorization from you to route 20% of traffic to fallback (non-ideal model).
- Short-to-mid: Request burst CPU/GPU headroom from capacity pool (ops authorization required). This will be a provisioning/authorization action and may take 8–12 minutes to realize.

Can you confirm whether GranitePay is OK with a temporary model-variant fallback for degraded quality? If so, we'll flip the routing for a canary and measure error reductions and latency.

Tessa Morgan
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference

Cc: bridge@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-22T09:03:00Z
Subject: RE: Hyperqueue investigation — initial findings and mitigation plan

Team — quick ops readout from infra/serving runtime:

- Cause (initial): a multi-tenant spike plus a noisy long-history batch job on the same dedicated rack triggered KV-cache thrashing and GPU memory churn. That caused a subset of pods to fall back into synchronous eviction/restart cycles which cascaded into the queue backlog.
- Impact: granitepay's reserved capacity was not fully honored because the serving mesh experienced intermittent node-level failures; requests were queued awaiting available KV-cache state.
- Current mitigation steps in-flight:
  * Rolling restart of 6/18 pods (targeted) to clear corrupted KV caches — ETA 10 minutes.
  * Enable prefix-KV isolation for granitepay traffic to reduce cross-tenant thrash (hotfix) — ETA 18 minutes with live testing.
  * Authorized a temporary routing rule to send 25% of granitepay traffic to a dedicated variant with 25% lower memory pressure (needs business approval from customer).

Ask: sales/CS (Tessa) to confirm whether the customer will accept model-variant fallback; if not, procurement/billing must approve immediate burst capacity allocation (request created: HubSpot 637182).

I will keep the bridge open and post kernel-level logs and pod-level metrics to the Jira ticket.

-David

Attachment: infra-kernel-notes-20280522.txt

From: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, david_kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-22T17:02:00Z
Subject: Exec summary & ask — Hyperqueue collapse impacting GranitePay (requesting burst authorization)

Vivek — escalating to you because GranitePay is a strategic reserved-capacity customer (DEAL-78341) and this incident risks SLA breach and potential downtime for payment flows. Short summary and asks below.

Summary:
- 08:05 UTC: sudden spike in multi-tenant usage + internal batch job caused KV-cache thrash on dedicated rack serving granitepay-prod.
- Result: subset of nodes entered an eviction/restart loop, causing per-reserved-pool queue depth to spike and sustained 5xx rates (~6% of requests) for ~45 minutes.
- Actions taken: targeted rolling restarts (in progress), prefix-KV isolation deployed (testing), routing to lower-memory variant staged (requires customer approval), bridge with infra & CS active.

Customer position: GranitePay is alarmed; they've requested either (A) immediate burst authorization to cover additional GPU headroom or (B) a temporary model-variant fallback which will lower quality but restore throughput. They prefer (A) if we can commit rapidly.

Asks (executive):
1) Approve an emergency burst authorization for up to 40% additional GPU headroom for the granitepay-reserved pool for the next 3 hours while we stabilize. This will incur overage exposure but prevents SLA penalty and potential churn.
2) If exec approval needed for financial exposure, authorize me to offer a goodwill credit if we exceed the committed spend threshold — I'll coordinate credit amount with finance.
3) Notify Legal if we need to document temporary routing changes or sign off on a short-term addendum.

If approved, infra will immediately provision burst nodes and we will shift traffic back from the lower-quality variant. Estimated time to recovery after approval: 9–14 minutes.

Attached: timeline note, customer error sample, links to Jira (INF-9182) and HubSpot record.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
